what_this_is: The render half of D7. Both `repo_hygiene` cases (ui-confidence-honesty, ui-confidence-honesty-regression) are STATIC READS of src/sec10k/web/static/index.html — no test in that harness issues an HTTP request, so nothing there can see a badge. This is the part only a browser can answer: does the qualifier appear beside a real confidence on a real filing, is the coverage line actually on screen, and does neither fire on a document where it would be false.

method.driver: the in-app browser tools (preview_start / computer / form_input / javascript_tool) against a live uvicorn server, driven by hand rather than by a committed script
method.why_not_a_script: D5's evidence is a re-runnable playwright script (tasks/reviews/d5_browser_walk.py). Playwright is not installed here and installing a browser toolchain is outside a display-only row; the measurements below are the same shape that script records (rect, checkVisibility, viewport intersection, text) and are reproducible by repeating the steps in `walk`.
method.server: uvicorn src.sec10k.web.app:app on 127.0.0.1:8011, served from a copy of this worktree in the session scratchpad
method.why_a_copy: this worktree lives under .claude/, which the preview sandbox cannot read — a server started there dies at `getcwd: Operation not permitted` before it executes anything. The harness also resolves .claude/launch.json from the MAIN repo, not from the worktree, so a launch entry added here is never seen. Recorded because it is the reason this walk was not started through preview_start's launch config; the served tree is an rsync of the branch under test, `evals/report` excluded.
method.visibility: every element verdict below uses BOTH `checkVisibility({visibilityProperty, opacityProperty, contentVisibilityAuto})` and a rect-vs-viewport intersection. PR #46 R2 established that `offsetParent` and a non-zero box are both true under `visibility:hidden`; PR #46 R6 established that `checkVisibility` answers RENDERED, not ON SCREEN, and is satisfied by an element parked at left:-9999px. Both questions are asked here.

walk.why: THE DEMO SHAPE. doc_status `success_with_warning`, carrying `unattributed_content` at 73%, and NO validator targets any item — so every item scored the unpenalised BASE_STRICT 0.95 and the side panel showed a column of bare 0.95s under a warned banner. This is postmortem §2's 'the UI amplified both' reproduced on a committed fixture.

verdict.panel_half: PASS, with one surface excluded by measurement rather than by assumption. Across cvx-2015 (20 items) and jpm-2024 (23 items), both warned documents, ZERO badges rendered a bare confidence and ZERO were clipped; across aapl-2025 (23 items), a clean document, ZERO badges rendered a qualifier. The PANE HEADER is a different story and is NOT covered by this PASS: at 1280 it renders `Part I · extracted · conf 0.95 …` on cvx-2015 and `Part IV · extracted · con…` on jpm-2024 item 15, showing none of the qualifier — identical to what the same band rendered before D7, so a pre-existing property of `.src-hdr`, carried as debt (Origin: D7).
verdict.banner_half: PASS — the figure is on screen (rect intersects the viewport, checkVisibility true) on the one walked fixture that carries `unattributed_content`, verbatim from validate.py's own message, with its caveat attached and, since PR #53 R7, under a label that names it as NON-coverage. Absent on both fixtures that do not carry it.

not_covered: One viewport only (1280x900). D5's layout row is what needs a width sweep; D7 changes no geometry — it lengthens two strings and adds one full-basis row to a flex container that already wrapped. The width-dependent consequence is the pane-header ellipsis, now measured on BOTH walked fixtures (PR #53 R5) and shown to be unchanged by D7.

Markdown and exclude-boilerplate modes were not driven. Both qualifiers and the coverage strip are computed from `doc_status`, `evidence.warnings` and `v.warnings`, none of which any view mode touches — but that is an argument, not a picture, and it is the same gap the standing D5-merge debt row records for that walk.

The fallback branch of `coverageStrip` (validate.py's message stops starting with a percentage, so the whole message is shown verbatim instead of an emphasised figure) was not exercised: no committed fixture produces it. It exists so the figure degrades to less emphasis rather than to silence.

is_this_a_D7_regression.method: Both fixtures' PRE-D7 header strings were fitted into the same bands with the same font, letter-spacing and text-transform, ellipsis width included.
is_this_a_D7_regression.reading: The rendered pane header is BYTE-IDENTICAL before and after D7 at both fixtures, because what a viewer sees in that band is decided by the band's width and not by the string's length — the band was already saturated by `Part … · extracted · conf …` on main. D7 lengthened a string that was already past the cut. So the item qualifier's absence from this surface is a pre-existing property of the `.src-hdr` band, not something this PR introduced, and the debt row says so.

badge_tokens_after_R3.why: PR #53 R3 — D7 first folded the document-level flag into `lo`, which repainted every badge on a warned document identically and erased the only item-level colour in the sidebar. The split is `lo` (amber TEXT, this item's own validators fired) vs `docw` (amber BORDER, resting dim text, this DOCUMENT is warned).

cvx-2015.reading: no validator targets any item on this filing, so no badge earns the item token and all 20 carry the document one. The demo's bare-0.95 column is still marked, just not marked as if a validator had fired.

badge_tokens_after_R3.clipping: Neither fixture clips a single badge: `scrollWidth == clientWidth` on every conf badge measured, including item 15's three-part string. The side panel — the surface D7's acceptance names — shows the whole qualifier at 1280 while the pane header shows none of it.
